newsitem.title: LEBANON: Two SLA militiamen killed in Lebanon blasts.
newsitem.headline: Two SLA militiamen killed in Lebanon blasts.

text.p: A pro-Israeli militiaman was killed in south Lebanon on Sunday in a roadside bomb explosion, hours after a captain in the militia died in a car bomb blast, pro-Israeli militia sources said.

They said the second blast occurred as the jeep carrying the South Lebanon Army commander of Jizzine rushed to the scene of the earlier attack in the village of Bkassine in Jizzine where 30-year-old SLA Captain Asaad Nammour died in a car bomb explosion.
A militiaman accompanying SLA commander Raymond Abu Mrad was killed. None of the other militiamen including the commander were hurt in the blast, the sources added.
Jizzine is a strip of territory officially outside Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone but under SLA control.
In Beirut, the pro-Iranian Hizbollah claimed responsibility for both attacks.

"The Islamic Resistance continues to hit hard with the aim of eliminating the remaining key agents following the instructions of the secretary general al-Sayyed (Sheikh) Hassan Nasrallah," Hizbollah said in a statement.

"Its fighters set off a roadside bomb as the car of the commander of the 20th batallion passed on its way to inspect the scene of the first operation which targeted Asaad Nammour. Those inside the car were killed or wounded," the statement added.
Pro-Israeli militia sources said guerrillas fired mortar bombs into the outpost of Kassarat al-Oroush in the eastern sector of the zone. There was no immediate report of casualties in the attack.
In retaliation, Israeli gunners shelled south Lebanese areas facing the outpost. There was no immediate word on casualties in the bombardment.
Hizbollah guerrillas regularly attack Israeli troops and their local militia allies in a bid to oust them from the 15-km (nine miles)-wide occupation zone.
